quotes.file: Sungbum/TSAD MA_STUDY OF ACCURATE PERCEPTION (SAUTRANTIKA SCHOOL)/TSAD MA RNAM 'GREL (PRAMANA VARTIKA)_A COMMENTARY ON ACCURATE PERCEPTION/DGE BSHES YE SHES DBANG PHYUG_GESHE YESHE WANGCHUK/S00030N_TSAD MA DGONGS RGYAN GYI SPAR BYANG SMON TSIG, LE'U GSUM PA BZHI PA_Colophon to 'The Jewel of the True Thought,' a Commentary on Valid Perception, Chapters 3-4_DGE BSHES THUB BSTAN RIN CHEN (@-@)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: རྣམ་འགྲེལ་ཚད་མའི་དགོངས་རྒྱན། ལེའུ་གསུམ་བཞིའི་སྤར་བྱང་སྨོན་ཚིག — the printers' colophon of Geshe Thubten Rinchen's Pramāṇavārttika edition (Sungbum, S00030N), the long recension of the same prose
quotes.why: The long recension of this colophon states the occasion the short one leaves out: the teaching in Tibet reduced to a mere name by the barbarians' ruinous conduct. Found by searching the Sungbum for the signatory's name.

quotes.file: Sungbum/TSAD MA_STUDY OF ACCURATE PERCEPTION (SAUTRANTIKA SCHOOL)/TSAD MA RNAM 'GREL (PRAMANA VARTIKA)_A COMMENTARY ON ACCURATE PERCEPTION/DGE BSHES YE SHES DBANG PHYUG_GESHE YESHE WANGCHUK/S00030N_TSAD MA DGONGS RGYAN GYI SPAR BYANG SMON TSIG, LE'U GSUM PA BZHI PA_Colophon to 'The Jewel of the True Thought,' a Commentary on Valid Perception, Chapters 3-4_DGE BSHES THUB BSTAN RIN CHEN (@-@)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: རྣམ་འགྲེལ་ཚད་མའི་དགོངས་རྒྱན། སྤར་བྱང་སྨོན་ཚིག — the same long recension, the first aim of the dedication
quotes.why: What 'without harm' (འཚེ་མེད) is set against: weapons of the atom and every kind of violent harm spreading day by day — the first item of the list that p426's སོགས abbreviates.

quotes.file: Sungbum/TSAD MA_STUDY OF ACCURATE PERCEPTION (SAUTRANTIKA SCHOOL)/TSAD MA RNAM 'GREL (PRAMANA VARTIKA)_A COMMENTARY ON ACCURATE PERCEPTION/DGE BSHES YE SHES DBANG PHYUG_GESHE YESHE WANGCHUK/S00030N_TSAD MA DGONGS RGYAN GYI SPAR BYANG SMON TSIG, LE'U GSUM PA BZHI PA_Colophon to 'The Jewel of the True Thought,' a Commentary on Valid Perception, Chapters 3-4_DGE BSHES THUB BSTAN RIN CHEN (@-@)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: རྣམ་འགྲེལ་ཚད་མའི་དགོངས་རྒྱན། སྤར་བྱང་སྨོན་ཚིག — the same long recension, the aims that lead into p426's opening clause
quotes.why: In the full text, p426's opening clause is the last item of a list — relighting the teaching in Tibet and spreading it in India come first — which is why p426 begins abruptly with ཅེས་འཛམ་གླིང and closes its purposes with སོགས; it also reads རྣམ་འདྲེན where p426 has རྣམ་འགྲེལ.

quotes.file: Sungbum/TSAD MA_STUDY OF ACCURATE PERCEPTION (SAUTRANTIKA SCHOOL)/TSAD MA RNAM 'GREL (PRAMANA VARTIKA)_A COMMENTARY ON ACCURATE PERCEPTION/DGE BSHES YE SHES DBANG PHYUG_GESHE YESHE WANGCHUK/S00030N_TSAD MA DGONGS RGYAN GYI SPAR BYANG SMON TSIG, LE'U GSUM PA BZHI PA_Colophon to 'The Jewel of the True Thought,' a Commentary on Valid Perception, Chapters 3-4_DGE BSHES THUB BSTAN RIN CHEN (@-@)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The same signature as p426 but preceded by the honorific mark ༧, which is what identifies ངག་དབང་བློ་བཟང་བསྟན་འཛིན་རྒྱ་མཚོ as the 14th Dalai Lama; p426 itself carries no mark.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་གཉིས་པའི་སྤྱི་དོན། — the printers' colophon at the end of the second-chapter volume of the same series
quotes.why: The short recension, in a sister volume of this very textbook series: ཅེས goes straight to ནང་བསྟན་གྲུབ་མཐའ་རིས་མེད, with no statement of aims at all. p426 is neither the short nor the long form but a middle one.

quotes.citation: མངོན་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་རྒྱན། — the printers' colophon appended to this edition of the root text, after the translators' colophon
quotes.why: The same middle recension as p426, word for word, except that it reads རྣམ་འདྲེན ('guide') where p426 reads རྣམ་འགྲེལ; nine of the thirteen printings of this recension in the corpus agree with it.

quotes.citation: འགྲེལ་པ་དོན་གསལ། — Haribhadra's closing verses, before the མཛད་བྱང and འགྱུར་བྱང
quotes.why: An author's own dedication of merit, for contrast: Haribhadra dedicates the merit of composing; the printers' verse and p426 dedicate the merit of printing, and sit after the translators' colophon, outside the work.

quotes.citation: འགྲེལ་པ་དོན་གསལ། — the close of the ten instructions, Abhisamayālaṃkāra chapter 1
quotes.why: Probe at the aligned place: the last passage the yig cha quotes before its colophon is this summary of Haribhadra's, and Haribhadra runs straight on from it into the twenty saṅgha — nothing in the Indian commentary closes here.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་མཐའ་དཔྱོད། — the closing formula before the printers' colophon
quotes.why: The companion mtha' dpyod on the same chapter ends with an authorial closing formula and a dedicatory verse before the printers' colophon; the spyi don volume, as this file has it, passes from Haribhadra's words straight to the printers.
